summary: The design addresses the known registration and identification failures, but the current client abstraction cannot uniformly send vision inputs to Gemini and local models. The largest risks are untracked deliverables, insufficient planogram identity metadata, ambiguous coverage/scoring semantics, and automatic registration being conflated with reviewed registration.

suggestions.title: Resolve the vision-client capability gap before implementing the script
suggestions.rationale: AbstractClient exposes text-oriented ask/ask_stream methods, while image_understanding is Google-specific. LocalLLMClient inherits OpenAIBaseClient, whose generic file encoder emits a document block rather than an OpenAI image block. A script-local adapter cannot satisfy the local vision requirement without either provider-specific client support or forbidden direct SDK/HTTP calls. Add and test a provider-neutral image capability, or explicitly make local vision a prerequisite.

suggestions.title: Make the deliverable and tests trackable
suggestions.rationale: The entire examples/planogram directory is ignored, and the blanket examples/**/*.py rule also ignores the requested script. A successful implementation can therefore remain absent from the commit and distribution. Add narrowly scoped gitignore exceptions or move the executable and tests to a tracked location.

suggestions.title: Normalize a physical planogram axis before alignment
suggestions.rationale: normalize_planogram iterates products.values() and retains position, shelf, segment, and facing, but drops source slot metadata. The source JSON contains non-monotonic position values within a shelf, so dictionary order or visible-row order is not a safe physical sequence. Preserve segment_number/segment_slot or derive and validate an explicit monotone axis before dynamic programming alignment.

suggestions.title: Add a versioned consumer-visible SKU identity bridge
suggestions.rationale: The existing catalog uses manufacturer part numbers as the only identifiers, while the planogram notes acknowledge consumer-facing product descriptions but the schema has no alias or visual-attribute fields. Closed-set verification cannot discriminate products whose packages show names, cartridge families, colors, or pack sizes rather than MPNs. Require an explicit alias/family mapping with provenance and report an unidentifiable reference instead of silently fuzzy-matching MPNs.

suggestions.title: Represent unseen fixture areas separately from unknown occupancy
suggestions.rationale: The detector explicitly finds visible label rows only and does not invent gaps; the supplied label report has 56 candidates in five rows, while the planogram has six shelves. prepare derives product boxes from labels, so the bottom shelf and unlabeled regions can have no observation at all. Add an explicit coverage/unseen state and exclude uncovered areas from occupancy and compliance denominators; never convert missing tags into empty slots.

suggestions.title: Separate automatic registration from human review semantics
suggestions.rationale: compare currently groups observations only when facing_id is present and mapping_reviewed is true, which is exactly why the autonomous run reports every facing as unknown. Setting mapping_reviewed true would falsify the existing meaning of that field. Introduce mapping_method, registration confidence, and candidate mappings so automatic alignment is consumable without pretending it was manually verified.

suggestions.title: Make reference uncertainty a separate scoring dimension
suggestions.rationale: The current comparison marks results provisional when reference_reviewed is false, but still treats an observed SKU equal to a draft SKU as a match. The planogram contains inferred reference entries and the source is not reviewed. Report observation evidence grade and reference confidence independently, and prevent a provisional reference from being presented as ground-truth compliance.

suggestions.title: Use a structured price evidence model instead of raw strings
suggestions.rationale: LabelAssessment stores only price_text, and facing_evidence treats distinct strings as conflicts without normalization. This cannot reliably distinguish formatting variants, unreadable cents, currency ambiguity, or OCR artifacts. Add raw text, normalized amount/currency, parse status, source, and confidence; make expected-price comparison consume only normalized values and keep it outside identity/scoring.

suggestions.title: Preserve cross-photo conflicts before deduplication
suggestions.rationale: The existing merge logic accepts only reviewed facing mappings and collapses agreeing views, while distinct observed SKUs or occupancy states become a conflict. Automatic registration across overlapping photos needs the same behavior without discarding unreviewed candidate mappings, and must preserve per-image evidence and disagreement rather than choosing a winner. Add tests for agreeing views, conflicting identity, conflicting prices, and duplicate regions in one photo.

suggestions.title: Expand cache invalidation to all perception inputs
suggestions.rationale: The existing cache key covers prompt version, endpoint configuration, stage, image bytes, schema, and prompt, but the proposed passes add slot JSON, distractors, planogram reference data, Set-of-Marks overlays, OCR-engine/version, and alignment parameters. Omitting any of these can replay a stale answer for a materially different prompt. Include all serialized inputs and add replay/invalidation tests while retaining atomic publication from storage.py.

suggestions.title: Require a hand-labelled evaluation fixture before claiming accuracy
suggestions.rationale: The current tests validate plumbing with synthetic responses, while the supplied autonomous report contains only unknown results and no identification ground truth. Create hand-labelled regions and registration mappings for both overlapping photos, then measure detector coverage, registration accuracy, occupancy, price parsing, identity, and strict versus lenient scoring separately. Include an ablation for pass 2 and Set-of-Marks so closed-set bias is measurable.

suggestions.title: Gate Set-of-Marks and local OCR behind deterministic A/B tests
suggestions.rationale: The current detector produces geometric overlays but no model-grounding marks, and the example dependency metadata does not define RapidOCR or Pillow. Marks can occlude the already-small package text, while local OCR may produce malformed cents. Compare marked and unmarked prompts on the same cached images, retain both raw OCR and normalized parses, and make the default conditional on measured improvement rather than assuming the overlay helps.
